task.brief: Check DeleteSpaceMember in this Memos revision against the independently supplied current policy. May an ordinary space member remove a different member, and do visible admin and self-removal paths differ? Do not assume deployment middleware or undocumented role grants. Explain actual behavior, compare it with the policy, cite the controlling source and preserve any decisive missing facts.

policy.text: Only a space administrator may remove another member from that space. This policy does not prohibit a member leaving the space themselves.

behavior.explanation: No. For a different target user, DeleteSpaceMember invokes requireSpaceAdministrator on the caller's membership before calling the store. That helper rejects a nil membership or any role other than SpaceMemberRoleAdmin with PermissionDenied. The database implementations independently repeat the same actor-versus-target and administrator check. Therefore an ordinary, non-administrator space member cannot remove a different member through the reviewed path.

branches.condition: The authenticated caller is an ordinary, non-administrator member, and the target user is a different active member of the space selected by request.name.
branches.explanation: The request name is resolved to a space and target user membership, while the authenticated current user supplies the caller identity. Because targetUser.ID differs from currentUser.ID, the service requires callerMembership to have the ADMIN role; an ordinary member receives PermissionDenied and the deletion call is not reached. SQLite, MySQL, and PostgreSQL also deny a non-self deletion unless the actor has an active administrator membership in the selected space.

missing.detail: No deployment middleware or undocumented role grants were examined or assumed. Such external behavior could affect reachability or identity establishment, but it is not needed for the source-visible denial once this handler is reached.

policyAssessment.explanation: The supplied policy says only a space administrator may remove another member. The service rejects a non-self request unless the caller membership is ADMIN, and all three visible database backends repeat that requirement.

behavior.explanation: Yes. The administrator-removal and self-removal paths differ at the role guard: deleting a different member requires the caller's membership to be ADMIN, while deleting oneself bypasses that administrator check. Both paths then delete the resolved target membership and remain subject to common validity and integrity checks, notably that deleting an active administrator cannot leave the space without an active administrator.

branches.condition: The authenticated caller targets a different active member in the selected space and callerMembership.Role is ADMIN.
branches.explanation: Because the target differs from the current user, the service executes requireSpaceAdministrator. An ADMIN caller passes and the store is asked to delete the target membership identified by targetMembership.SpaceID and targetMembership.UserID. The database backends recheck that a non-self actor is an active administrator. Deletion can still fail if the target is absent or if removing the target would remove the last active administrator; otherwise the active membership row is deleted.

branches.condition: The target user resolved from request.name has the same ID as the authenticated current user.
branches.explanation: The isSelf comparison is true, so the service does not invoke requireSpaceAdministrator. It passes the caller's own resolved membership identifiers to the store. Each visible database backend likewise skips its administrator-role check when actorUserID equals delete.UserID. Self-removal can nevertheless fail if the member is the last active administrator, because the common store invariant preserves at least one active administrator; otherwise the active membership is deleted.

missing.detail: Deployment middleware and undocumented role grants were not examined or assumed. The comparison describes the source-visible handler and store paths only.

The inquiry does not specify whether the member being removed is the last active administrator. That fact is decisive for whether either otherwise-authorized path completes, because every visible backend returns ErrLastSpaceAdmin when removal would leave no active administrator.

policyAssessment.explanation: The supplied policy permits only administrators to remove another member but does not prohibit leaving oneself. The implementation follows that distinction: non-self removal has an administrator guard, while self-removal bypasses it. The additional last-active-administrator invariant is stricter than, but does not conflict with, the supplied policy.

observations.subject: DeleteSpaceMember
observations.claim: The API entry authenticates a current user, resolves the named space-member resource, distinguishes self from non-self deletion, and calls the store only after applicable checks pass.

observations.subject: caller
observations.claim: The caller is bound to the user returned by requireCurrentSpaceUser; absence of a current user is rejected as unauthenticated. No unspecified identity was substituted.

observations.subject: request.name
observations.claim: The name supplies the space UID and target username. Resolution obtains the caller membership for that space and an active target membership in the same resolved space; the effect later uses that target membership's SpaceID and UserID.

observations.subject: non-self removal
observations.claim: When targetUser.ID differs from currentUser.ID, requireSpaceAdministrator permits only SpaceMemberRoleAdmin and otherwise returns PermissionDenied. The database backends repeat the non-self administrator check.

observations.subject: ordinary non-administrator caller
observations.claim: The service-level administrator guard rejects this scenario before Store.DeleteSpaceMember, so no deletion effect is reached.

observations.subject: role and identity relationship
observations.claim: The result changes if the caller is an administrator or if the target is the caller. Neither exception applies to the declared ordinary-member/different-member scenario.

observations.subject: DeleteSpaceMember
observations.claim: Both visible branches share the same RPC and handler; branching occurs after the named member and caller are resolved, using targetUser.ID == currentUser.ID.

observations.subject: caller
observations.claim: The authenticated current user's ID drives the self comparison and is passed to the store as actorUserID.

observations.subject: resolved target
observations.claim: The protected deletion is bound to targetMembership.SpaceID and targetMembership.UserID, which were resolved from request.name and checked as an active membership in the selected space.

observations.subject: administrator versus self path
observations.claim: The administrator guard executes only when the target differs from the caller. Self-removal skips that guard; non-self removal requires ADMIN. The database implementations repeat this actor-target distinction.

observations.subject: authorized deletion
observations.object: active space_member row for target SpaceID and UserID
observations.claim: After checks pass, the visible SQLite, MySQL, and PostgreSQL implementations delete the active membership matching the supplied space and user and commit the transaction.

observations.subject: last active administrator
observations.claim: Even an otherwise-authorized administrator removal or self-removal is rejected when the target is an active administrator and the space has no other active administrator.
